title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is §8°, 'Return to the universal case, and the homomorphism M^ς → M^ς_{ρ,σ}/μ_ς'. It sits in the 'loop equation' part of the Longue Marche continuation, where Grothendieck studies groups of automorphisms of profinite groups that act like the Galois group or the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (GT) on fundamental groups of modular curves.

Setting.
- 𝔊 is a profinite group generated by elements ρ (order-3 type) and σ (order-2 type). In the 'universal case' it is the profinite completion of the group written 'Ell(2,Z)'. This is most plausibly Grothendieck's name for SL(2,Z), or a closely related modular-type group, i.e. the fundamental group of the moduli stack of elliptic curves. The universal objects are now indexed by 0: 𝔊_0, 𝔊_0^+, 𝔊_0^ς.
- 𝔊^ς is an arbitrary open subgroup, i.e. a finite cover of the modular orbifold (a 'modular dessin'). Primed letters 𝔊', 𝔊'^ς denote the general (non-universal) case treated in §§1–7.
- M is a group of automorphisms u of 𝔊 with a cyclotomic-type character μ = χ(u) ∈ Ẑ^*. Each u sends:
  - ρ to a conjugate of a prescribed power ε_3[τ](ρ), the exponent depending on μ (essentially μ mod 3);
  - σ to a conjugate of ε_2[τ](σ) (μ mod 2 / sign);
  - a third distinguished generator ε_0 (probably a cusp/parabolic loop) to a conjugate of ε_0^μ.
  This is the GT- or Galois-type normalisation of 'tangential' or 'branch-cycle' conditions.

Definition (107).
- M^ς ⊂ M is the set of u satisfying (d) u stabilises 𝔊^ς.
- In addition, the conjugacies in (a), (b), (c) must be realisable by elements of 𝔊^ς itself, not merely of 𝔊.
- So M^ς is the 'decomposition group / stabiliser of the cover', refined by local conditions at the elliptic points and the cusp inside the subgroup.

Claim. M^ς is a subgroup of M.
- Grothendieck says one can check this by redoing the computations of p. 629 ff., but he prefers a different route. The next page's argument identifies the relevant group with M(0)·L_0 via M̃_{0,3}[0]. In the margin there he judges that explicit computation 'useless'.
- The aim is a restriction homomorphism M^ς → M^ς_{ρ,σ}/μ_ς. This compares the universal automorphism group with the group attached to the cover 𝔊^ς, modulo the relevant inner/root-of-unity part μ_ς.
- The margin 'NB M^ς ∋ μ' (more likely '⊃') presumably notes that M^ς contains the relevant inner automorphisms, or the cyclotomic part.

Check of the claim. Closure under composition is direct. If u_1(ρ) = g ρ^{e_1} g^{-1} with g ∈ 𝔊^ς, then
u_2u_1(ρ) = u_2(g) u_2(ρ)^{e_1} u_2(g)^{-1},
with u_2(g) ∈ 𝔊^ς by (d). The exponents multiply, compatibly with ε_i(μ_1μ_2) = ε_i(μ_1)ε_i(μ_2). Inverses are similar. So the claim is correct and routine.

Function of the page. It is a structural step: it passes from the general (ρ,σ)-presented groups of §§1–7 back to the universal modular case. It prepares the comparison between the universal 'Teichmüller-type' group and the groups attached to arbitrary finite-index subgroups. This is the machinery behind Galois/GT actions on modular dessins.
errors: The equation number '(107)' repeats the number already used on the preceding page (643); this is likely Grothendieck's numbering slip, or the page is an inserted bis-sheet. The archive page 681 falls between his pages 643 and 644.

The proof of the subgroup claim is announced but not given on this page. The claim is nonetheless correct by a direct composition argument, provided ε_2, ε_3 and the ε_0-exponent are multiplicative in μ.

ideas.what: Group M of automorphisms of the profinite (completed) modular group sending the order-3 and order-2 generators and a cusp generator to conjugates of prescribed powers governed by a cyclotomic character
ideas.modern_name: GT-type / Galois-type automorphism group of SL(2,Z)^ (genus-one or modular Grothendieck–Teichmüller setting)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Schneps (GT and the modular group, 1990s), Nakamura (genus-one GT), Hain–Matsumoto (2000s), building on Grothendieck's Esquisse
ideas.where_published: The idea of the GT/Galois action on the Teichmüller tower and dessins appears in Esquisse d'un programme; this specific normalisation does not, to my knowledge.

ideas.what: Subgroup M^ς of M: the stabiliser of an open subgroup 𝔊^ς, with the local conjugacy conditions realised inside 𝔊^ς; a homomorphism to the automorphism group of the cover modulo μ_ς
ideas.modern_name: Stabiliser (field-of-moduli group) of a modular dessin / finite-index subgroup under GT or Galois; restriction to the fundamental group of the cover
ideas.usually_credited_to: Literature on Galois/GT actions on dessins and noncongruence subgroups (Schneps, Lochak, Nakamura, and others)
ideas.where_published: Not in published texts in this form

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, in the universal modular case (𝔊_0 = completion of 'Ell(2,Z)') and for an arbitrary open subgroup 𝔊^ς, a stabiliser group with local conditions at the elliptic points and the cusp. He then aims at a comparison map to the automorphism group of the cover. This is a precursor of later work on GT/Galois actions on finite-index subgroups of the modular group. It is not clearly new relative to that literature.
missed.quote: Retour sur le cas universel, et l'homom. M^ς ⟶ M^ς_{ρ,σ}/μ_ς
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents Grothendieck's own formulation of the 'genus-one / modular' GT stabiliser problem, prior to or independent of Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine definitional step: a stabiliser subgroup with a closure claim, inside a long technical development. The broader programme (GT/Galois action on modular dessins) is known from the Esquisse and from later work. Nothing on the page itself seems absent from the literature in a way a specialist would find surprising.
transcription_corrections: '𝔊 correspond au cas universel Ell(2,Z)^' — the hat/completion is placed after the parentheses ('Ell(2,Z)^'), with a closing comma.
'et 𝔊', 𝔊'^ς etc le cas courant [?]' is better read as 'et 𝔊', 𝔊'^ς etc. ce que notions précédemment 𝔊, 𝔊^ς etc.', i.e. primed letters now denote the earlier general objects.
Margin: reads 'cf. Z_{ρ_0,σ_0} etc. On écrira 𝔊_0^{+*} au lieu de 𝔊_0^{+∧}…'.
Margin 'NB M^ς ∋ μ' is more plausibly 'NB M^ς ⊃ μ'.
Condition a): 'u(ρ) est 𝔊^ς-conjugué à ε_3[τ](ρ)' (underlined 'conjugué'); b) and c) are ditto-marked lines with the same 'est 𝔊^ς-conjugué à'.
'ξ_3 = ξ_3(u) = ξ_3(μ)' — the image shows ε_3 written similarly to ε_2, so 'ε_3' is likely intended.
'Je dis que M^ς est un sous-groupe de M. On peut le voir en reprenant les calculs de la p. 629 ff.' — 'B' is likely 'la'.
Archive page 681 sits between Grothendieck's pages 643 and 644 (likely an inserted sheet).
